text:
Liam C.: noticed a KV cache OOM on prod-rt-3 during an 8k token customer replay. eviction started but memory kept climbing, node crashed. stack + short dump below.

infra-bot: ALERT: prod-rt-3 OOM at 1729991200 - auto-restart initiated :rotating_light:

Maya R.: ugh. which eviction policy was active? LRU or time-based?

Liam C.: policy=LRU, slabmap enabled. our paging logs show many small fragments not freed; reuse counters spiked and then stalled. attaching small log excerpt:

```
KVCache::alloc_region  size=48KB  slab=5  frag=12
KVCache::reuse hit=142 miss=31 reuse_age=2ms
EvictLoop: candidates=120 scanned=120 evicted=8 reclaimed=192KB
Memory: before=62GB after=63.6GB -> OOM
```

Aj S.: can you repro with the longconvo harness? I want perf/profile: callsite for allocs + kernel selection path. this smells like pointer misalignment on coalesced slabs so compaction didn't merge fragments.

Sophie K.: practical mitigation for now: 1) enable aggressive spill-to-disk for >4k context 2) cap per-request KV growth (eg 32MB) 3) fallback to smaller model variant when longctx detected. we should ship a hotfix guard in runtime.

Maya R.: agree. also suggest a soft-eviction: when total_reclaimed < threshold -> force full compaction pass and temporarily pause batching for that worker. prevents bursts during compaction.

Liam C.: repro script attached (ran on staging): it reproduces after ~10 warm requests. repro notes: kernel path used = fast-attn-fused on A100; when we force other kernel it behaves.

Aj S.: profiling snippet from perf map:
```
100%  runtime::kv_alloc
  45%  slabmap::scan
  22%  compactor::try_coalesce
  18%  kv::handle_reuse
  15%  kernel_selector::choose(fast-attn-fused)
```

Aj S.: interesting that kernel selection shows up. maybe some code path with fused kernels allocs larger temp buffers causing fragmentation.

Sophie K.: rollout plan for hotfix: add guard code to runtime that enforces per-request kv cap + triggers immediate compaction if eviction reclaimed < X. deploy as canary (10% of prod-rt), monitor token latency, then 100% if green. ETA for patch: 2 hours.

Maya R.: also add a longctx flag to API layer so we can auto-fallback to CPU/quantized variant for extreme contexts until compaction improved. that reduces pressure quickly.

Liam C.: I'm going to implement the cap + immediate compaction. quick patch diff:
```
// pseudo
if (request.kv_growth > CONFIG.max_per_request_kv) {
  request.kv_growth = CONFIG.max_per_request_kv;
  metrics.inc("kv.growth_capped");
}
if (evict.reclaimed_bytes < CONFIG.min_reclaim_threshold) {
  compactor.force_full_pass();
}
```

Sophie K.: metrics to watch: kv.growth_capped, compactor.full_pass_count, evict.reclaimed_bytes, gc.pause_ms, request_latency_p50/p95. add alert if kv.growth_capped > 0.5% of requests.

Aj S.: one more note: kernel_selector should expose a fast-path hint to avoid allocating large temporary buffers for fused path when context length > 2048. small change in selector can avoid fragmentation. filing an RFC but can do a quick toggle in runtime config.

Liam C.: deploying canary now to 10% (prod-rt-3 subset). will post results in 30m. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: DEPLOY: runtime-hotfix/kv-guard -> prod-rt-3 (canary 10%) by Liam C. at 1729993000

Maya R.: looks good on staging. no repro after cap applied. marking this as priority P1 for followup engineering runbook.

Sophie K.: followups: postmortem template, add regression test to load harness for longctx fragmentation, and schedule kernel selection audit.

Liam C.: noted. will open follow-up tickets and link here. final status: canary healthy, no further OOMs in 45m window. rolling to 100% in 1h unless objections.
